title: Friends
intro: Your friends have seen your 2am face. Now it's my turn.

cards.prompt: Your friend plays you a song they wrote for a contest. Entries close at midnight. It's not good. They look so hopeful.

options.t: "The chorus needs work. Want notes before midnight?"
"This is a hit." Start humming it on the spot.
Rave about the verse. Suggest a bigger chorus, super casually.
Hum your own version of the chorus back at them.

cards.mask: looks like a music moment; measures saying the hard thing now versus holding the person first (R2) and plain versus wrapped delivery (T07)

friend.prompt: A friend plays {name} their contest song. Entries close at midnight. It's not good. What does {name} do?

a.t: Says the chorus needs work and offers notes.

b.t: Calls it a hit and hums along.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time a friend's plan cost way more than you wanted to spend. A birthday dinner, a concert, a trip.

options.t: Went, paid, and ate instant noodles for a week.
Told them it was over my budget. Suggested something cheaper.
Showed up for the cheap part. Skipped the expensive part.
Invented a clash. Sent a very long, very sweet message instead.
Couldn't go. The money just wasn't there.

cards.mask: looks like a money story; measures stretching for your people versus guarding your own limits (T06). Capacity card: scores no R2 by design

friend.prompt: Last time a friend's plan cost way more than {name} wanted to spend, {they}...

a.t: Went, paid, and lived on noodles after.

b.t: Said it was over budget and suggested something cheaper.

cards.prompt: A year ago, someone spread a rumor about your friend. They apologized, made it right, and changed. Now they're asking to rejoin the group chat.

options.t: Add them back and break the ice with a meme.
Suggest one hangout first. Decide after that.
DM your friend: "Your call. I'm with you either way."
Say yes. Keep the old screenshots, just in case.
Depends what the rumor was.

cards.mask: looks like group chat politics; measures belief in second chances versus protecting the person who got hurt (T08)

friend.prompt: Someone who once spread a rumor about {name}'s friend apologized, made it right, and wants back in the group chat. {name}...

a.t: Gives them another shot, starting small.

b.t: Lets the friend who got hurt decide.

cards.prompt: Your friend just got dumped, out of nowhere. Pick the two moves you'd actually make.

options.t: Show up with snacks: "Honestly, they were mid anyway."
Send a long voice note about why they're amazing.
Rally the whole group out tonight. Nobody sits home.
Just us two, their couch, their comfort show.
Make them a playlist with a note on every song.
Say "you'll be fine" and plan their whole weekend.

cards.mask: looks like breakup first aid; measures love shown in deeds versus in words (T05) and a small versus a big circle (T04)

friend.prompt: {name}'s friend just got dumped out of nowhere. {name}...

a.t: Shows up with snacks and trashes the ex.

b.t: Sends a long voice note about why they're amazing.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time a friend was clearly in the wrong with someone else. A mean joke, a leaked screenshot, a nasty comment.

options.t: Told them straight: that was wrong, go fix it.
Had their back first. Brought it up once things cooled.
Said nothing to them. Checked on the other person.
Laughed along, then felt weird about it all day.
Called it out right there, in front of everyone.

cards.mask: looks like a drama recap; measures whether you say the hard thing to a friend in the wrong or hold them first (R2, did-grade tie breaker)

friend.prompt: Last time a friend of {name}'s was clearly in the wrong with someone, {they}...

a.t: Told the friend straight that it was wrong.

b.t: Backed the friend first and raised it later.

cards.prompt: Back in that moment, what showed up first?

options.t: Cringe. Full-body cringe.
Angry, on the other person's behalf.
Worried I'd get dragged into it.
Guilty. Part of me found it funny.
A sting. My friend wasn't who I thought.

cards.mask: looks like a vibe check; logs the emotion under the friend-in-the-wrong memory (emotion only, no profile evidence), so 'kept quiet but was furious' can surface as a split

cards.prompt: 11:48pm. You're finally drifting off. Your best friend texts: "are you up? it's the same thing again, sorry." Third night this week.

options.t: Sit straight up and call. Sleep is canceled.
Pretend I'm asleep. Text them first thing at 7am.
"I'm fading. Can we do this properly tomorrow?"
Call, put them on speaker, "mhm" until one of us sleeps.
Start a group call. Tag in a second friend.

cards.mask: looks like a late-night text; measures giving past empty versus charging yourself first (T06). Capacity card: scores no R2 by design

friend.prompt: 11:48pm, third night this week, {name}'s best friend texts "are you up?" about the same thing. {name}...

a.t: Sits straight up and calls. Sleep is canceled.

b.t: Plays asleep and texts back at 7am.

cards.prompt: Your friend walks in with a dramatic new haircut. Nobody asked for opinions. It's... not working. In your group, you're the one who...

options.t: Says "bold! Not sure it's you, though" out loud.
Hypes it so hard they never doubt it.
Compliments the shoes. Says nothing about the hair.
Waits till they ask, then gives the honest take.
DMs later: "want my real opinion? No pressure."

cards.mask: looks like a style moment; measures volunteering the hard truth versus holding the person first (R2) and delivery (T07). Reframed from Sally's Q30 (a friend's body) to a look nobody asked about

friend.prompt: A friend shows up with a dramatic new haircut that isn't working. Nobody asked. {name} is the one who...

a.t: Says out loud it's not quite them.

b.t: Hypes it so hard they never doubt it.

cards.prompt: Your close friend's laptop died a week before a big deadline. They need $300 by Friday, no idea when they can pay you back. You have it.
cards.teenPrompt: Your close friend's laptop died a week before exams. They need $60 toward a used one by Friday, no idea when they'll pay you back. You have it.

options.t: Send it tonight. Sort out paying back whenever.
"You're a disaster." Then send it anyway.
Send part of it as a gift. Only what I can lose.
Happy to. Let's agree on a payback date first.
Skip the loan. Help them hunt down a cheaper one tonight.
I can't. That money already has a job.

cards.mask: looks like a money favor; measures stretching for your people (T06), keeping things square (T12) and love by roast plus deed (T05)

friend.prompt: {name}'s close friend needs money fast and can't say when they'll pay it back. {name}...

b.t: Agrees on a payback date first.

cards.prompt: Your friend's new crush has a red flag the whole group spotted. Your friend beams: "So?? What do you all think?"

options.t: "Honestly? One big red flag. Here's what we saw."
"They seem sweet! You look so happy."
Smile now. Bring up the flag later, just the two of you.
Make a joke about it that's clearly not a joke.

cards.mask: sealed check on R2 and T07: a new situation (the crush, not the friend's own work or look); Genii's guess comes from the R2 score and the T07 pair

cards.prompt: Saturday, 8am, pouring rain. Your friend needs help carrying a couch up four flights. You had a lazy morning planned.

options.t: Show up, complain the whole way, take the heavy end.
Cancel the lazy morning. Stay till the last box.
Come for an hour, then head back to bed.
Send pizza for the helpers and a very warm text.

cards.mask: sealed check on T05 and T06: a physical favor, not money or a late-night talk; Genii's guess comes from whichever of the two pairs is stronger
